attractions.name: Angkor Wat
attractions.desc: The largest religious monument in the world, built in the 12th century as a Hindu temple before later becoming Buddhist. Its five central towers, representing the peaks of Mount Meru, are among the most recognizable silhouettes in Southeast Asia, especially at sunrise. A single visit barely scratches the surface of its carved galleries and reflecting pools.

attractions.name: Angkor Thom & the Bayon
attractions.desc: The last great capital of the Khmer Empire, its central Bayon temple famous for over 200 massive serene stone faces gazing out in every direction. The South Gate approach, lined with rows of carved figures, sets the tone before reaching the temple itself. It sits within walking or biking distance of Angkor Wat.

attractions.name: Ta Prohm
attractions.desc: Left largely as it was found, this temple has been partly reclaimed by the jungle, with massive silk-cotton and strangler fig tree roots wrapping over its stone walls and towers. It gained wider fame as a filming location for Tomb Raider. The combination of ruin and living forest makes it one of the most photographed sites at Angkor.

attractions.name: Tonlé Sap Lake
attractions.desc: Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake, which dramatically expands and contracts with the seasons, supporting floating villages that rise and fall with the water level. Boat trips from Siem Reap pass stilted houses, floating markets, and fishing communities adapted to this unusual rhythm. It offers a different, more everyday view of Cambodian life than the temples.

attractions.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum
attractions.desc: A former high school converted into a prison and interrogation center during the Khmer Rouge regime, now preserved as a memorial and museum. Rooms of photographs of victims and preserved cells offer a direct, unflinching account of a period that killed roughly a quarter of the population. It's a difficult but widely considered essential visit.

attractions.name: Royal Palace, Phnom Penh
attractions.desc: The official residence of the King of Cambodia, its golden spires and manicured grounds sit beside the Silver Pagoda, named for its floor of solid silver tiles. It offers a lighter counterpoint to the capital's more sobering historical sites. Modest dress is required to enter the grounds.

itinerary.label: Days 1–4
itinerary.title: Siem Reap & Angkor
itinerary.desc: Sunrise at Angkor Wat, the Bayon's faces, Ta Prohm's tree roots, and a Tonlé Sap boat trip.
itinerary.cost: A 3-day Angkor Archaeological Park pass costs $62; a sunrise tuk-tuk transfer runs $15–20.
itinerary.food: Try amok at a local restaurant in Siem Reap — the steamed version in a banana leaf is the traditional presentation.

itinerary.label: Days 5–7
itinerary.title: Phnom Penh
itinerary.desc: The Royal Palace, riverside promenade, and the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum.
itinerary.logistics: ~40min flight or 6h bus from Siem Reap
itinerary.cost: The Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum costs $5–6 to enter; the Royal Palace costs about $10.
itinerary.food: Try num banh chok for breakfast, a genuine local morning tradition rather than a tourist dish.

goodToKnow.tipping: Small tips appreciated for guides and drivers; USD is widely used alongside riel
goodToKnow.safety: Generally safe; stick to marked paths around temple ruins
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Buses connect main towns; tuk-tuks and bikes work well for exploring Angkor
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Siem Reap International Airport (REP) or Phnom Penh International (PNH) both work as gateways, depending on which city you'd rather start in

food.name: Amok
food.desc: A creamy coconut curry, traditionally made with fish, steamed in a banana-leaf cup.

food.name: Khmer red curry
food.desc: A milder coconut curry with lemongrass, potatoes, and a choice of protein.

food.name: Num banh chok
food.desc: Rice noodles served cold with a green fish-based curry sauce, a popular breakfast dish.

food.name: Kampot pepper dishes
food.desc: Dishes built around Kampot's famous peppercorns, prized for their bright, floral heat.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Cambodia?
faq.a: Yes, most nationalities need either an e-visa, applied for online in advance, or a visa on arrival — both straightforward and inexpensive.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Siem Reap (REP) or Phnom Penh (PNH), depending on which city you'd rather start in.

faq.q: How many days do I need at Angkor?
faq.a: At least 2–3 full days to see the main temples (Angkor Wat, Bayon, Ta Prohm) without rushing; a multi-day pass is worth it over a single-day ticket.

faq.q: Can I pay in US dollars in Cambodia?
faq.a: Yes, USD is used interchangeably with Cambodian riel almost everywhere — riel is typically only used for small change.

daysReason: 8 days covers Siem Reap/Angkor and Phnom Penh at a comfortable pace. 4–5 works for just Angkor; 10+ lets you add the coast around Sihanoukville.
visa: An e-Visa or visa on arrival is available for most nationalities — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Angkor Wat
attractions.desc: O maior monumento religioso do mundo, construído no século XII como templo hindu antes de mais tarde se tornar budista. As suas cinco torres centrais, representando os picos do Monte Meru, contam-se entre as silhuetas mais reconhecíveis do Sudeste Asiático, especialmente ao amanhecer. Uma única visita mal arranha a superfície das suas galerias esculpidas e piscinas refletoras.

attractions.name: Angkor Thom e o Bayon
attractions.desc: A última grande capital do Império Khmer, com o seu templo central Bayon famoso por mais de 200 enormes rostos de pedra serenos a olhar em todas as direções. A abordagem pelo Portão Sul, ladeada de fileiras de figuras esculpidas, dá o tom antes de chegar ao próprio templo. Situa-se a uma curta distância a pé ou de bicicleta de Angkor Wat.

attractions.name: Ta Prohm
attractions.desc: Deixado em grande parte como foi encontrado, este templo foi parcialmente reconquistado pela selva, com enormes raízes de figueira estranguladora e sedeiro a envolverem as suas paredes e torres de pedra. Ganhou fama mais ampla como local de filmagem de Tomb Raider. A combinação de ruína e floresta viva torna-o um dos locais mais fotografados em Angkor.

attractions.name: Lago Tonlé Sap
attractions.desc: O maior lago de água doce do Sudeste Asiático, que se expande e contrai dramaticamente com as estações, sustentando aldeias flutuantes que sobem e descem com o nível da água. Passeios de barco desde Siem Reap passam por casas sobre estacas, mercados flutuantes e comunidades piscatórias adaptadas a este ritmo invulgar. Oferece uma visão diferente e mais quotidiana da vida cambojana do que os templos.

attractions.name: Museu do Genocídio de Tuol Sleng
attractions.desc: Uma antiga escola secundária convertida em prisão e centro de interrogatório durante o regime do Khmer Vermelho, agora preservada como memorial e museu. Salas com fotografias de vítimas e celas preservadas oferecem um relato direto e sem rodeios de um período que matou cerca de um quarto da população. É amplamente considerado uma visita difícil mas essencial.

attractions.name: Palácio Real, Phnom Penh
attractions.desc: A residência oficial do Rei do Camboja, com os seus pináculos dourados e jardins bem cuidados junto à Pagode de Prata, batizada pelo seu chão de telhas de prata maciça. Oferece um contraponto mais leve aos locais históricos mais pesados da capital. É exigido vestuário modesto para entrar nos terrenos.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–4
itinerary.title: Siem Reap e Angkor
itinerary.desc: Nascer do sol em Angkor Wat, os rostos do Bayon, as raízes de árvore de Ta Prohm, e um passeio de barco no Tonlé Sap.

itinerary.label: Dias 5–7
itinerary.title: Phnom Penh
itinerary.desc: O Palácio Real, o passeio à beira-rio, e o Museu do Genocídio de Tuol Sleng.
itinerary.logistics: ~40min de voo ou 6h de autocarro desde Siem Reap

itinerary.label: Dia 8
itinerary.title: Partida
itinerary.desc: Voa a partir de Phnom Penh.

goodToKnow.tipping: Pequenas gorjetas são apreciadas para guias e motoristas; o dólar americano é amplamente usado ao lado do riel
goodToKnow.safety: Geralmente seguro; mantém-te nos caminhos marcados à volta das ruínas dos templos
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Autocarros ligam as principais cidades; tuk-tuks e bicicletas funcionam bem para explorar Angkor
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Siem Reap International Airport (REP) or Phnom Penh International (PNH) both work as gateways, depending on which city you'd rather start in

food.name: Amok
food.desc: Um caril cremoso de coco, tradicionalmente feito com peixe, cozinhado a vapor numa taça de folha de bananeira.

food.name: Caril vermelho khmer
food.desc: Um caril de coco mais suave com erva-príncipe, batatas e a proteína à escolha.

food.name: Num banh chok
food.desc: Noodles de arroz servidos frios com um molho de caril verde à base de peixe, um prato popular ao pequeno-almoço.

food.name: Pratos com pimenta de Kampot
food.desc: Pratos construídos à volta da famosa pimenta de Kampot, apreciada pelo seu picante brilhante e floral.
